https://discord.com/channels/14357864699.summary: Can't speak for the true 1999 classic era, but at least by Velious, playing a tank was great. At least as a career paladin.
https://discord.com/channels/14357864699.sourceText: Can't speak for the true 1999 classic era, but at least by Velious, playing a tank was great. At least as a career paladin. One problem though was the cultural zeitgeist telling tanks to stack HP to the exclusion of all else. As a tank, I'd get asked my HP before being invited to groups. This persisted up into PoP. I looked at the math though, realized that was wrong, and started minmaxing for AC. I'd get a tell asking my HP, and my response would be, "Forget the HP; I'm the single highest AC character on the server, let me show you what that does." And then an hour of grinding later, the cleric would be like, "Hey, how come I barely have to heal you? I'm actually kinda bored." Today we take it for granted that AC is the god stat, but the perception was different back then. Most tanks were straight up playing the game wrong because everyone told them to.
